recaps.ending: Arthur's coalition liberates Free Hive of the Waves, ends the active control over its surviving victims, and recovers many stolen eggs. The victory does not kill the Mindsinger. Brixaby's bond and nullification divert its attempt to seize Arthur, forcing it into a Scourge-rotted white dragon that escapes with followers, eggs, and a hidden legendary card. Digger reunites with his rider and helps relocate refugees to Island Free Hive. Laird returns to Mesa Free Hive to develop a volunteer defense force, while Cressida, Joy, Horatio, and Sams remain together and intend to rejoin Arthur later. At Wolf Moon Hive, Whitaker accuses Arthur of undermining command, but Valentina accepts his decision to leave. Brixaby identifies their recovered legendary card as Call of the Heart. Arthur and Brixaby intentionally trigger Return to Start, obscure their trail through Mesa, and follow the seeker's map through a portal to a kingdom on the far side of the world. They hope its unknown target will strengthen the wider fight against the Scourge.
recaps.in_short: Arthur and Brixaby are abducted to Mesa Free Hive, where they discover a society outside kingdom rule and prepare to confront the escaped Mindsinger. After finding Mesa's hidden combat-card library, they survive an emissary attack that kills Shadow, and Brixaby consumes the captured legendary weapon and grows large enough to carry Arthur. They repel an invasion, only to learn that the Mindsinger has stolen dragon eggs across several hives to harvest cards from hatchlings. Arthur unites Mesa volunteers with Wolf Moon forces, frees controlled victims, and reaches the operation's center. Brixaby prevents the Mindsinger from taking Arthur's body, but the enemy escapes inside a corrupted white dragon with eggs, followers, and a legendary card. The surviving eggs are recovered and the damaged hive evacuated. Arthur rejects Wolf Moon's political future, recovers Call of the Heart, and deliberately escapes with Brixaby. Its map sends them through a portal toward an unknown resource in a distant kingdom, while Cressida, Joy, Horatio, and Sams plan to follow.

recaps.text: Previously: Arthur, traveling under the name Ernest Kane, became linked to the tiny legendary dragon Brixaby and acquired extraordinary cards centered on learning skills and consuming cards. His true Rowantree heritage places him amid a dangerous family dispute involving his father Calvan, his uncle Lionel, and his cousin Pennrow. Baron Kane remains tied to Arthur's assumed identity and the danger facing the borderlands, while Second claims an unresolved debt against him. At Wolf Moon Hive, Arthur formed important connections with Cressida and her dragon Joy, as well as Horatio and Sams. He also became entangled with senior leaders Valentina and Whitaker. Most urgently, Arthur and Brixaby helped release the Mindsinger, a mind-controlling Scourge entity that remains at large. Their responsibility for that escape, the enemy's unknown plans, and the struggle over Arthur's legendary powers all carry into this book.

So far this book: Four months into rider training, Arthur leads a class exercise that turns dangerous when Maurice injures Lilac. He removes the offending pair and accepts responsibility just as the class is sent to a major eruption at Guardian City. Valentina orders the trainees to prioritize noble card stores, but Arthur redirects them to rescue trapped civilians. Their improvised defense succeeds at a cost, leaving several pairs injured. A quest then draws the remaining group toward Noble Woodmore's card library. Brixaby senses danger before they land, and Arthur warns a Blood Moon trio away from the courtyard. The estate explodes, killing that trio and scattering the class. Riderless dragons emerge from a protected crater, capture Cressida and Joy, and seize Arthur, Brixaby, and Shadow as well. Arthur recognizes one red dragon from his childhood, but the abductors' purpose and destination remain unknown.

Arthur's party wakes in Mesa Free Hive, a hidden desert settlement beyond kingdom control. Chablis and Laird hold them as constrained guests, using enchanted locks to suppress Arthur's abilities. The free hive supports humans and dragons as independent workers, relies on practical cards, and reveals that other settlements survive outside the kingdoms. Laird explains that he once refused a forced rider link and that he placed Arthur's legendary Master of Skills card in the border village. He wanted to keep it from Baron Kane and acted on a prediction that the gift would later benefit him. Arthur also tells Cressida the truth behind his cover: Ernest Kane is Arthur Rowantree, son of the former Duke Rowantree. Cressida accepts why he hid his identity. Both begin considering what Mesa's social model offers, although the council remains divided over whether Arthur and Brixaby are allies, assets, or threats.

Mesa Free Hive gives Arthur's group limited freedom. Brixaby apprentices under Dimitri as a chainmail worker, while Len and his rider voluntarily join the settlement after describing how Wolf Moon treated lower-ranked pairs as expendable. During a card-gifting ceremony, an assassin strikes at Arthur. Joy intercepts the poisoned blade and survives only by absorbing rare necrotic and nullification cards, which leave her with a dangerous green forelimb and venomous claws. Brixaby secretly takes the assassin's stealth-class card, allowing Arthur to copy its practical skills. Arthur also studies Mesa's agriculture with Flossie, tests unusual plants, and stores psychic-blocking apples. When the council questions the attack, the cardless assassin compulsively calls Arthur Rowantree a liar. Arthur infers that the Mindsinger may be influencing another free hive. Arthur, Brixaby, and Cressida agree that they helped create this danger and must grow stronger before confronting it.

After two months at Mesa, Arthur and Brixaby earn rare shards while expanding their skills. Brixaby develops chainmail craft, uncovers Mesa's secret trade in weapons and armor, and uses a secondary core to copy the assassin's stealth class before passing that card to Cressida. The group completes a rare metal-control combat card for Arthur, giving his chainmail rivets a second use as projectiles. Their search for Mesa's hidden combat cards takes them into a secured underground complex. They avoid a trapped armory, take books on enchantment and rune security, and discover maps showing that surviving kingdoms and free hives are isolated amid Scourge territory. A requisition letter names Call of the Heart, a legendary card that may belong to the same set as Brixaby's Call of the Void and may be at risk of destruction in a seeker enchantment. A concealed map points toward Mesa's combat cache, while Joy's quest redirects the group into a dungeon whose rules and rewards remain uncertain.

Arthur, Brixaby, Cressida, and Joy enter a constructed wave dungeon guarding Mesa's combat-card library. Repeated attacks push their stamina, mana, and defenses close to failure. Arthur studies enchantment under stopped time, and Brixaby transfers part of Cressida's fire card into metal bars, giving each fighter a compatible fire enhancement. Laird and a teleporting companion join the later waves, admitting that they also want combat cards because Mesa's council trades such cards away instead of arming its defenders. After the group clears the trial, Arthur uses his personal storage to bring everyone into the reward room. They take a limited selection from a large but incomplete library. On leaving, they meet four dragons controlled by the Mindsinger. The scarlet emissary unleashes legendary sound magic that kills Shadow, and the card's backlash leaves its wielder dying. Laird, Cressida, Joy, and Brixaby defeat the yellow and blue attackers, but the brown dragon remains alive and the legendary card is not yet secured.

Brixaby consumes the recovered legendary sonic card through Call of the Void. While he sleeps through the change, he grows into a more mature dragon large enough to carry Arthur. The timing leaves the group vulnerable when agents of the Mindsinger demand Mesa Free Hive's surrender. Chablis attempts to pay tribute with combat cards, but the emissaries open a portal for an invasion force. Laird reveals a concealed combat retinue, and Arthur distributes cards from the hidden library to civilian volunteers. Fighting beside Mesa's new defenders, Arthur uses his mental shield to free one controlled attacker, then copies mana and portal magic to collapse the enemy gateway. The awakened Brixaby catches Arthur as he falls from the closed portal.

Arthur and Brixaby move defenders through a temporary portal and break the enemy formation shaping a vast saltwater flood. Brixaby's stunning shout disrupts the attackers, and the defenders collapse the wave before it reaches Mesa. Arthur orders captures where possible, allowing him to release several dragons from the Mindsinger's control. The victory immediately reveals a larger loss: every dragon egg in Mesa has been stolen, along with nesting mothers, and the experimental gardens have been poisoned. Arthur restores the captured brown dragon by grounding him in memories of his rider and gains a Deprogramming skill in the process. The dragon identifies himself as Digger and explains that his rider is a hostage. Reports of matching raids at other free hives support Arthur's conclusion that the Mindsinger is using stolen eggs and hatchlings to produce rare cards. Despite Chablis's objections, Mesa begins organizing willing card holders into a mobile defense force, and Arthur decides to seek help from the kingdom hives.

Arthur leads Mesa volunteers to Wolf Moon Hive under worsening political conditions and an unnatural blizzard. Horatio and Sams, who believed Arthur dead, rejoin him. Arthur warns Whitaker, Valentina, and Buck Moon's leader that the Mindsinger has raided multiple hidden nests and is farming cards from stolen hatchlings. Wolf Moon agrees to intervene, although Buck Moon refuses. Valentina privately gives Arthur her Subtle Influence card and acknowledges earlier manipulation around his cards and the king. She also warns that Whitaker is positioned to dominate Wolf Moon after her death. Arthur rejects the future expected of him within the hive's hierarchy.

The assault on Free Hive of the Waves begins in confusion as unprotected Wolf Moon fighters fall under the Mindsinger's influence. Arthur uses Mind Block anchors as projectiles to free controlled riders and dragons, while Sams, Laird, and the Mesa volunteers help his retinue advance. Whitaker retreats after losing control of part of his force, but Arthur continues into the infected hive. Digger opens an underground route where the group finds stolen eggs, controlled nesting mothers, and evidence of mass hatchling deaths. Arthur frees mothers and organizes the evacuation of eggs before pressing toward the operation's center. There the Mindsinger attacks through a Scourge-rotted white dragon and card-bearing scourgelings. Its reserve shimmer dragons nearly overwhelm the party, but Arthur weakens the mind attack with a psychic-blocking apple. When the Mindsinger tries to exchange minds with Arthur, Brixaby's bond and nullification divert the spell into the white dragon. The Mindsinger escapes in that body with eggs and followers, while Arthur's side captures a legendary card from a fallen defender.

The Mindsinger's remaining thralls recover after its retreat, and healers stabilize the Scourge Rot. Arthur returns stolen cards where possible, distributes others, and seals the hatchling-killing chamber as the Tomb of Hatchlings. Free Hive of the Waves is evacuated because the lingering damage makes it unsafe. Digger reunites with his rider and leaves Arthur's retinue to assist the refugees at Island Free Hive. Laird returns Mesa's surviving eggs and stays to build its volunteer defense. Cressida, Joy, Horatio, and Sams remain alive and plan a separate journey before joining Arthur again. At Wolf Moon, Whitaker accuses Arthur of misleading the hive and undermining command. Arthur tells Valentina that he will leave rather than accept Wolf Moon's political path, though he still intends to strengthen the war against the Scourge. Brixaby reveals that their recovered legendary card is Call of the Heart. They deliberately trigger Return to Start to escape, then use the seeker's map and copied portal magic to travel to an unfamiliar kingdom on the far side of the world. The Mindsinger remains alive in a corrupted white dragon, carrying eggs, followers, and another legendary card.

recaps.ending: Arthur, Brixaby, Cressida, Joy, Horatio, Sams, Soledad, Equinox, Marion, and Asha escape New Houston's Darkheart. Arthur learns that Darkhearts are traps maintained by scourge gods, gathering the cards of dead delvers until they can erupt beneath the settlement above. New Houston's sheriff agrees to discourage deeper delves but cannot close the site without provoking unrest, and Arthur is barred from entering again. Arthur leaves with Master of Cards, five additional heart-deck spaces, and a repaired rare trio that supports card restoration. Soledad is bonded to Equinox. Marion repairs his heart at the cost of his former legendary benefits and bonds to the origin hatchling Asha. He must now attempt to heal King Eleazar under the mythic dragons' protection. Claude remains missing after his cards are found among the bandits' possessions. Arthur and Brixaby plan to watch New Houston briefly, pursue the remaining legendary cards, and eventually return to Wolf Moon Hive. The Mindsinger conflict, Mesa Free Hive's defense, Wolf Moon politics, the Rowantree claim, and Arthur's other inherited enemies remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: Arthur and Brixaby reach New Houston, a city built around a managed Darkheart, and earn entry to its reshuffling while fighting organized Scourgeling threats in the surrounding Scourge Deadlands. Arthur's card anchor is destroyed during a dispute over a major harvest, but he recovers its cards and learns that nearby nests grow around buried dragons and decaying cards. Reunited with Cressida, Joy, Horatio, and Sams, he enters the early-ripening Darkheart alongside Marion and Soledad. Personalized trials yield new powers, two dragon eggs, and evidence about the origins of cards. After bandits attack their territory, Soledad bonds with Equinox, while Marion's damaged heart initially prevents his bond with Asha. Mythic dragons reveal that Darkhearts are scourge-god traps designed to harvest delvers' cards and eventually destroy their cities. Arthur completes his legendary Master set with Master of Cards and expands his heart deck. Marion repairs his heart, bonds with Asha, and accepts a mission to heal King Eleazar. The party escapes, but New Houston's eventual eruption remains unresolved.

recaps.text: Previously: Arthur and Brixaby are linked rider and dragon, carrying legendary power while facing several unresolved conflicts. The escaped Mindsinger remains a major Scourge threat, operating through a corrupted white-dragon body with followers, eggs, and a legendary card. Wolf Moon Hive is politically divided. Valentina supports Arthur, while Whitaker remains a rival connected to his earlier training. At Mesa Free Hive, Laird is working to improve the settlement's defenses, but Chablis has reservations about a more combat-focused course. Arthur's family position is also unsettled. His cousin Pennrow Rowantree is a rival legendary holder and claimant, his father Calvan is vulnerable near the border, and his uncle Lionel remains a threat. Arthur's use of the Ernest Kane identity ties him to Baron Kane, whose debts drive an interest in Arthur's legendary card. A hostile carded associate known as Second also claims Arthur owes him for a rescue, despite having tried to kill him. These political, family, and personal dangers remain active as Arthur and Brixaby begin their next journey.

Arthur and Brixaby arrive outside a foreign walled city where the language, transport systems, and constant Scourgeling danger are unfamiliar. Border officer Domingo admits Arthur after hearing his cover story, and Arthur helps the guards defeat an unusually powerful attacker. Inside, Arthur trades valuable enchanting knowledge for instruction in Texan, allowing both partners to communicate locally. They learn that New Houston stands above a Darkheart that suppresses ordinary eruptions and periodically opens for a reshuffling, where delvers can seek cards and other rewards. Arthur and Brixaby decide to enter. Their public flight draws official attention, but the city instead hires them to help answer the growing attacks. Undersheriff Lopez sends them along the Scourge Deadlands road, where they save one caravan from a large flock and learn that children from another wagon group are still missing. Arthur and Brixaby find the destroyed wagons and uncover an underground shelter holding survivors. The rescue proves to be bait: rare Scourgelings have waited nearby for someone to expose the concealed group.

Arthur evacuates the children into his personal space and discovers that much of the apparent rare force is an illusion. He kills the true illusion wielder and secretly takes its card, but suffers a severe wound. At the hospital, Marion helps secure treatment and conceals the card from the sheriffs. Arthur releases the rescued children and receives a reward, only to lose it immediately to his medical bill. Soledad Boudreaux, a cardless survivor who protected younger travelers, asks to pursue dragon riding with him. Arthur bargains with Over-Sheriff Walker for five early reshuffling places in return for guiding an expedition to the rare Scourgelings. The force includes Lopez, the Lightning Cats, and Claude, an inventive utility specialist. Their search reveals a fissure producing Scourgelings and a concealed rare nest. Most adventurers treat it as a harvest opportunity despite Arthur's warning. When the battle begins, an earthquake drops combatants and monsters into a deep pit, revealing that the rare Scourgelings prepared a mass-casualty trap.

Arthur and Brixaby help rescue survivors from the pit while Claude burns many trapped Scourgelings. Bradley ends the battle with toxic gas, then exploits the sealed area to claim nearly every valuable corpse. Arthur enters the gas to challenge him, temporarily removes Bradley's three rare cards, and forces a fair distribution. Holding those cards catastrophically damages Arthur's card anchor. During the later auction he nevertheless steals and consumes Endless Grindstone, a utility card that accelerates learning, and collapses. Hospital specialists find that the shattered anchor has wounded his soul and cannot safely be replaced for at least a year. Brixaby returns to the nest and discovers living spawn and hidden shards beneath it. Arthur learns that the anchor's cards still exist and uses card shuffling to extract them, but his heart deck has only one free space and cannot hold the recovered set. The pair now have several loose cards, a damaged soul, no safe anchor, and evidence that the supposedly defeated nest continues producing Scourgelings underground.

Arthur and Brixaby locate more nests in the Scourge Deadlands and discover buried dragon corpses beneath them. Decaying cards left in the bodies appear to sustain the nests and their regenerating spawn. A silver dragon yields three damaged rare cards concerned with repairing cards, understanding them, and working with shards. Arthur lacks room to use the trio and fears worsening his soul injury, so Brixaby stores them. Daniel helps the pair rent a secluded barn and trade lesser cards for supplies. Ravi, a healer with exceptional heart-deck insight, advises Arthur to respect his soul's resistance to a new anchor. He suggests that the Darkheart may instead let Arthur rearrange or expand his natural deck. Arthur trains meditation for that attempt. Cressida, Horatio, Joy, and Sams then arrive after a punishing crossing of the Deadlands, still fighting a large airborne flock. Arthur and Brixaby join the battle, reunite with their allies, and provide food and water. The expanded group clears another nest, finds another dead dragon and decaying card, and strengthens Arthur's belief that preserving damaged cards may help prevent new Scourgelings.

Guided meditation helps Arthur identify Master of Cards as the missing legendary card in his set and as his goal within the Darkheart. Brixaby finally advances his crafting by creating art rather than merely useful equipment, gaining the Blacksmith Artist class. Arthur prepares a delve with Brixaby, Cressida and Joy, Horatio and Sams, Marion, and Soledad. He distributes rare cards, reveals his existing Master cards, and trains neglected practical skills. The group studies the Darkheart's shifting, individualized dangers, but its opening arrives two days earlier than predicted. Over-Sheriff Walker warns that it is close to eruption and asks strong delvers to relieve its magical pressure. The party gathers equipment and healing supplies, sets an escape point outside the city, and descends by dragon amid a disorderly crowd. Inside, a legendary force asks Arthur what he needs. When he answers Master of Cards, the force separates him from Brixaby and strips away most of his usual options, beginning a private trial while the other members are also divided into challenges tailored to them.

The preliminary Darkheart trials reward each member differently. Arthur advances his Cooking class through an endless hostile kitchen. Brixaby fights through a foundry, Joy develops her intuition in a labyrinth, Soledad rescues hatchlings while gathering blank shards, Marion develops medical judgment, Cressida earns a new summon, and Horatio and Sams refine their control of light. Reunited, the party claims a territory and splits again. Joy's intuition sends Arthur alone into a Utility challenge that resembles a technological society facing the first spread of the scourge. Arthur teaches bunker survivors how to assemble blank shards into cards and sees cards become a defense against airborne rot, though he cannot know whether the scenario is literal history. When the bunker falls, he escapes with three rare medical cards and two blank dragon eggs. Meanwhile, Brixaby leads the Combat group on a volcanic island. The group defeats a lava-covered rare, but a false legendary reward enthralls Brixaby until Joy exposes the illusion trap. The combat team secures additional rare cards, and both groups return to their territory with their rewards.

Arthur gives Marion the three rare healing cards, and the group feeds blank shards into the two eggs. One becomes a red egg suited to Soledad, the other a luminous silver egg suited to Marion. A bandit group then breaches the territory, demands the party's resources, and tries to abduct Soledad. Brixaby loses control under Berserker's Rage, but the retinue recovers and kills the attackers after their leader breaks a surrender. Among the captured cards Arthur finds some belonging to the missing Claude, though the discovery does not establish Claude's fate. Marion uses the rare Material Dungeoneer card to build a nest. Soledad's red hatchling bonds with her, but Marion's silver hatchling cannot link because his heart still bears damage from former legendary power. Arthur refuses to abandon the bond. Marion opens a limited route toward the core for Arthur, Brixaby, Cressida, Horatio, the silver hatchling, and himself, while the others defend the territory with Soledad's hatchling, Equinox. The descending team reaches a gemmed door and passes into crushing spiritual pressure before a scourge god.

Mythic dragons intervene against the scourge gods and explain the Darkheart's true purpose. Its escalating challenges collect cards from dead delvers, letting the trap grow until an eruption destroys the city above. They protect Arthur long enough to attempt one final challenge in return for his agreement to resume leadership at Wolf Moon Hive and send Marion to treat King Eleazar. Arthur faces an illusion of Pennrow Rowantree, accepts responsibility for his own wrongs without yielding to fear, and wins five new heart-deck spaces. He takes Master of Cards, completing a legendary three-card set and gaining advanced control over decks and cards. Marion uses the challenge's wish to repair his heart, losing the remnants of his old legendary benefits. The silver origin hatchling then chooses healing power, bonds with him, and takes the name Asha. The party escapes before the mythics' protection fails. Days later, Arthur repairs the damaged rare meta-card trio and begins developing as a Card Smith. He warns New Houston's sheriff about the trap, but the city cannot close it without unrest. Arthur cannot enter again. Claude remains missing, and the eventual eruption is only delayed as Arthur and Brixaby prepare to pursue their remaining legendary cards.
